title: Chain-Centric protocol action space
detail: Content agents are restricted to publish_chain, attack, revise_chain, or pass. Free-form agreement and conclusion-only rebuttal are invalid actions.

title: Step-level attack requirement
detail: An attack must target a specific chain and step. Vague disagreement or unsupported conclusion-level rejection is rejected by protocol validation.

title: Evidence-pool citation rule
detail: Reasoning steps and attacks must cite evidence from the evidence pool. Missing or external references can be rejected or marked as requiring evidence acquisition.

title: Zero-attack claims are not consensus
detail: Claims with no attacks should be marked as unscrutinized rather than accepted as consensus, regardless of their apparent evidence independence.

title: Coordination layer avoids LLM-as-Judge
detail: The coordination layer should use observable behavior such as attacks, revisions, survival, evidence references, and symbolic state stabilization rather than asking an LLM judge to choose the winner.

title: Claim-level microbiome test reached natural stabilization
detail: A 5-agent fixed-input microbiome obesity test with claim-level evidence ended at round 41 with SYSTEM_STATE_STABILIZED, 34 claims, 73 chains, 79 attacks, 45 evidence items, 14 active chains, 39 broken chains, and 20 archived chains.

title: Prior self-audit collapsed overclaims
detail: A previous self-audit run reached SYSTEM_STATE_STABILIZED at round 44 with 64 attacks, 23 evidence items, 23 claims, 36 chains, and 22 broken chains; the main conclusion was that overclaims were attacked rather than automatically protected.

title: Observed limitation: claim duplication
detail: In the claim-level microbiome test, many semantically similar claims were created around the same issue, suggesting weak claim canonicalization and a need for semantic merge or clustering controls.

title: Observed limitation: evidence layer dependency
detail: The protocol's epistemic value depends on evidence-pool quality. Dynamically added evidence can re-open disputes, and unverified or over-broad evidence can pollute downstream claims.
